name: South Australia
summary: A British blue ensign with a yellow disc in the fly showing a piping shrike (Australian magpie) with wings outstretched on a branch.
origin: South Australia's earlier badge (1876–1904) showed Britannia with a seated Aboriginal man. The piping shrike badge was adopted in 1904.

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: The rising sun behind the bird.

symbols.name: Piping shrike
symbols.description: A black and white white-backed magpie on a gum tree branch.

facts: The 'piping shrike' is an old name for the white-backed Australian magpie.
The yellow disc represents the rising sun.
clues: A blue ensign with a black and white bird on a branch inside a yellow disc.
Its bird is known by an old name, the piping shrike.
Its disc is the rising sun.
